reasons.plan: Zaxara's X-spell trigger is backed by only Divergent Equation and Wildwood Scourge, and a thin +1/+1 counter subtheme (Terrasymbiosis, Level Up, Cytoplast Root-Kin, Zameck Guildmage) is diluted by off-plan cards like Cowabunga!, Mindreaver, Foundry Inspector and Accursed Duneyard.
reasons.fit: There was no request, so fit is not graded.
reasons.mana: Forty-five lands is far too many for a curve where 26 of 54 nonland cards cost two or less, and five of the nonbasics (Accursed Duneyard, Archaeological Dig, Eldrazi Temple, Shrine of the Forsaken Gods, Cactus Preserve) are colorless, tapped, or one-shot for colour, though the even 13/13/13 basic split covers all three colours.
reasons.ramp: There are about seven ramp pieces (Simic Signet, Commander's Sphere, Darksteel Ingot, Sanctum Weaver, Verdant Eidolon, Market Festival, Case of the Locked Hothouse), plus Hazel of the Rootbloom and Zaxara herself, which is adequate given the huge land count.
reasons.draw: The deck has many small draws (Harmonize, Brilliant Spectrum, Treasure Hunt, Confirm Suspicions, cycling cards, and sacrifice-to-draw artifacts like Scroll of Avacyn and Golden Egg), but its only real repeatable engines are Terrasymbiosis and Zameck Guildmage.
reasons.interaction: It has a solid spread of answers, including counterspells (Neutralize, Vex, Voidslime, Confirm Suspicions, Keep Safe), removal (Befoul, Frogify, Grave Peril, Tower of Calamities), and resets in Do or Die and Inundate.

details.summary: This is an unfocused Sultai pile that barely uses Zaxara's X-spell trigger and runs a bloated, partly colorless 45-land mana base. It is held up by decent interaction and some card flow.

reasons.plan: The deck is a loose mono-red aggro and artifact pile with many off-plan cards like Apocalypse Chime, Havoc, Hand to Hand, Accursed Duneyard and Tsabo's Web, and little that feeds the commander's sacrifice ability.
reasons.fit: Pia and Kiran Nalaar is the commander, but only a handful of cards (Ravenous Robots, Magic Pot, Golden Egg, Foundry Inspector) support sacrificing artifacts or making artifact tokens, so the build follows the request in name only.
reasons.mana: Thirty-nine lands is high for a curve centred on 2-3 mana, and Eldrazi Temple, Shrine of the Forsaken Gods and Accursed Duneyard add little, though mono-red colour is never strained.
reasons.ramp: Only Commander's Sphere, Darksteel Ingot, Luck Bobblehead, Golden Egg, Foundry Inspector and the unreliable Bucknard's Everfull Purse count as ramp, which is thin even for a modest curve.
reasons.draw: Card flow is limited to small one-shot cantrips like Golden Egg, Scroll of Avacyn, Fountain of Renewal, Tsabo's Web and Commander's Sphere, plus the looting from Gate to the Afterlife, with no real engine.
reasons.interaction: Spot removal includes Jaya's Greeting, Thundering Rebuke, Wild Slash, Engulfing Flames, Blood Feud, Chainflinger and Wojek Embermage, and Whipflare and Destructive Force act as sweepers, but nearly all of it is creature-only damage.

details.summary: This is an unfocused mono-red pile that barely uses Pia and Kiran Nalaar's artifact-sacrifice engine, with too many lands, weak ramp and draw, and filler cards that do nothing in Commander; its burn-based removal is the only real strength.

reasons.plan: Around 25 artifacts give Pia and Kiran some sacrifice fodder, but many cards serve no plan (Apocalypse Chime, Dawn-Blessed Pennant, Havoc, Storm Cauldron, Rift Elemental, Hand to Hand), so the deck reads as a loose red pile.
reasons.fit: Roughly half the nonland cards are artifacts, including Ravenous Robots, Foundry Inspector and Golden Egg, but few of them build on each other, so the artifact theme is only partly realised.
reasons.mana: With 46 lands for a mostly 2-3 mana curve, the deck has far too many, and Eldrazi Temple, Shrine of the Forsaken Gods, Accursed Duneyard and the symmetrical Storm Cauldron add little.
reasons.ramp: There are only about four acceleration pieces: Commander's Sphere, Darksteel Ingot, Luck Bobblehead, and one-shot Golden Egg or Magic Pot treasure.
reasons.draw: It has only small one-shot cantrips (Golden Egg, Tsabo's Web, Scroll of Avacyn, Fountain of Renewal, Commander's Sphere, the Voldaren Epicure Blood token) and no real engine.
reasons.interaction: Removal is plentiful but almost all damage aimed at creatures (Jaya's Greeting, Thundering Rebuke, Wild Slash, Whipflare, Chainflinger, Tower of Calamities), with clumsy resets in Destructive Force and Decree of Annihilation and nothing for enchantments or artifacts.

details.summary: A nominal artifacts deck with a reasonable amount of creature removal, held back by 46 lands, very little ramp or draw, and many filler cards that don't support Pia and Kiran.

reasons.plan: A clear Zombie recursion plan with about 25 Zombies, lords like Cemetery Reaper and Diregraf Captain, and graveyard payoffs, though off-plan cards like Lightshell Duo, Zhalfirin Shapecraft, Liliana's Talent and Grimoire of the Dead dilute it.
reasons.fit: The deck leans hard on Zombie creatures and self-mill (Mire Triton, Unseal the Necropolis, Geralf's Mindcrusher) that Gisa and Geralf can recast, but Zombie Apocalypse destroys the Human commander and some cards ignore its engine.
reasons.mana: Only 27 lands is below the 30 floor for a curve with 17 cards at five or more mana, and six of the duals enter tapped (Salt Marsh, Submerged Boneyard, Temple of Deceit, refuges).
reasons.ramp: Seven pieces (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Dimir Signet, Talisman of Dominance, Commander's Sphere, Hedron Archive, Wayfarer's Bauble) is middling and doesn't make up for the low land count.
reasons.draw: Plenty of flow, including repeatable sources like Undead Augur, Midnight Reaper, Vampiric Rites, Spark Reaper and Laboratory Drudge alongside Pilfered Plans, Deep Analysis and Distant Melody.
reasons.interaction: Flexible answers abound: Murder, Fell, Cut Down, Feed the Swarm, Counterspell, Sinister Sabotage, Undermine, plus resets in Necromantic Selection, Consuming Tide and Aetherize.

details.summary: A well-stocked Zombie recursion deck with strong draw and interaction that suits Gisa and Geralf, but its 27-land mana base with many tapped duals is a serious liability.

reasons.plan: Most cards serve a Kangee flyers attack plan, with anthems like Empyrean Eagle, Favorable Winds, Steel-Plume Marshal and Gravitational Shift, but filler such as Phyrexian Censor (which taxes its own spells), Lightshell Duo, Samite Herbalist, Whiskervale Forerunner and White Sun's Zenith drifts off-plan.
reasons.fit: The deck is clearly a flyers deck, with over 30 flying creatures, flying anthems and flyer payoffs like Tide Skimmer and Windreader Sphinx, though a handful of ground cards dilute it.
reasons.mana: Only 26 lands is well under the 30 minimum for a curve with 26 cards at four or more mana, and seven of them (including Coastal Tower, Sejiri Refuge, Tranquil Cove and Temple of Enlightenment) can enter tapped.
reasons.ramp: There are about seven ramp pieces (Azorius Signet, Talisman of Progress, Commander's Sphere, Sky Diamond, Hedron Archive, Wayfarer's Bauble and Warden of Evos Isle), plus land-to-hand fetchers that don't really accelerate, which is middling for a deck this short on lands.
reasons.draw: Plentiful draw includes repeatable engines like Bident of Thassa, Tide Skimmer, Windreader Sphinx, Dawn of Hope and Staggering Insight alongside Sphinx's Revelation, Winged Words, Distant Melody and Skyscanner.
reasons.interaction: It has over 15 flexible answers, including Counterspell, Absorb, Sinister Sabotage, Prayer of Binding, Hanged Executioner, Crush Contraband and Condemn, plus the board resets Cleansing Nova, Time Wipe and Aetherize and protection from Surge of Salvation.

details.summary: This is a focused Azorius flyers deck with excellent card draw and interaction, but its 26-land mana base is dangerously thin and will often stall its many four- and five-drops.
